title: Global derived Hom, derived sections and internal dual for stratum modules
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $X$ be a scheme and let $R_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ be its pulled-back coefficient ring on the small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A_X$ be the category of internal $R_X$-module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A_X)$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For $M\in\mathcal A_X$, define the global derived Hom functor $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(M,-):D(\mathcal A_X)\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ to be the unbounded right derived functor of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_X}(M,-)$, valued in abelian groups. On a K-injective representative $I^\bullet$ this is the complex with degree-$q$ term $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_X}(M,I^q)$ and differential postcomposition with $d_I$, equivalently the global Hom complex with source $M[0]$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. Define $R\Gamma(X,-)=R\operatorname{Hom}_X(R_X,-)$, where $R_X$ is the regular module. This is the derived global sections convention of [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], before taking zeroth cohomology: under the canonical section-action equivalence from internal modules to sectionwise module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], the regular module corresponds to the unit sheaf, and global sections is $\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(R_X,-)$. Finally, for $L\in\mathcal A_X$ define $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{R_X}(L,R_X)$ using sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom], equivalently the internal Hom from $L$ to the tensor unit. These are definitions; no support-adjunction theorem, admissibility or local freeness is assumed.

The cited ringedSiteZerothHypercohomologyOfUniverses is the same right-derived Hom-from-unit convention, in the sectionwise presentation, followed by H^0. sectionModuleEquivalence identifies the regular module with the unit sheaf by identity on sections/actions and identifies Hom complexes termwise; its exactness preserves K-injectives.
